acv.quote: Ninety-five K ACV, on a two-year term.

data.reason: The CFO, whom we never met, compared only our per-transaction rate against the bank's sharpened rate and saw 'the same thing,' because nothing from us put a figure on what Fernbrook's failed orders were costing. Sam blames price, but he skipped Farah's offer to value their declines and sent the deck when Lucy asked for a business case.

trigger.action: Aim messaging at ecommerce leaders whose large orders fail at checkout and who can't get an answer from their processor on why.
trigger.quote: She said about one in twelve online orders was failing at the payment step, and it was worse on the big baskets.

decider.action: Write a CFO-facing message the champion can carry alone, showing what failed orders cost next to the rate difference, since the CFO won't meet vendors.
decider.quote: Lucy said he doesn't take vendor meetings and she'd carry it.

competitor.action: Pre-empt an incumbent bank's rate cut by moving the comparison early from the per-transaction rate to total cost, including gateway fees and chargeback handling.
competitor.quote: After the bank came back, every email was the rate.

message.action: Keep the explanation of why big-ticket orders get declined, and stop using the average acceptance-uplift slide as the value proof; replace it with the customer's own numbers.
message.quote: When our solutions engineer, Farah, explained why big-ticket orders get knocked back and what we do about it, Lucy was nodding the whole way.

proof.action: Build a one-page business case template, filled from the customer's three-month decline export, that prices their failed orders for the CFO.
proof.quote: Lucy asked once if we had something she could hand Martin. Like a one-page business case.

words.action: Use 'orders dying at the last step' and 'the big baskets' in messaging instead of 'declines' and 'acceptance uplift'.
words.quote: we do all the work to get someone to buy a four-thousand-dollar greenhouse and then the card says no.
